# Gemini Project - Email Editor

This document outlines the project of creating a web-based email editor using Vue.js and the Unlayer editor.

## User Story

As a user, I want to be able to create and edit email templates using a drag-and-drop interface. I should be able to save my templates and load them back into the editor. I also want to be able to use merge tags and design tags to personalize my emails.

## Key Features

- **Vue.js Framework**: The application will be built using Vue.js 3.
- **Unlayer Editor**: The core email editing functionality will be provided by the Unlayer editor.
- **Vite Tooling**: The project will use Vite for fast development and builds.
- **TypeScript**: The project will be written in TypeScript for better code quality and maintainability.
- **Backend Server**: A backend server will be created to handle saving and loading of email templates.
- **Database**: A database will be used to store the email templates.
- **Merge Tags**: The editor will support merge tags to personalize emails.
- **Design Tags**: The editor will support design tags to apply consistent branding to emails.
- **File Manager**: The editor will include a file manager to upload and manage images.
- **Saved Blocks**: The editor will allow users to save and reuse content blocks.

## Project Setup

The project will be set up as a monorepo with the following structure:

- `frontend`: The Vue.js application.
- `backend`: The backend server.

## Getting Started

To get started with the project, you will need to have the following installed:

- Node.js
- pnpm

Once you have the prerequisites installed, you can run the following commands to get the project up and running:

```
pnpm install
pnpm dev
```

This will start the frontend development server and the backend server. You can then access the application in your browser at `http://localhost:5173`.

## Next Steps

The next steps for the project are to:

- Implement the backend server to save and load email templates.
- Implement the database to store the email templates.
- Implement the merge tags and design tags functionality.
- Implement the file manager functionality.
- Implement the saved blocks functionality.
- Write tests for the application.
- Deploy the application to a hosting provider.

## Contributions

Contributions to the project are welcome. Please feel free to open an issue or submit a pull request.

## License

This project is licensed under the MIT License. See the `LICENSE` file for more information.

// This is your Prisma schema file,
// learn more about it in the docs: https://pris.ly/d/prisma-schema

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

model MergeTag {
  id          String   @id @default(uuid())
  key         String   @unique
  label       String
  defaultValue String
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
}

model DesignTag {
  id         String   @id @default(uuid())
  key        String
  value      String
  templateId String
  template   Template @relation(fields: [templateId], references: [id])
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt  DateTime @updatedAt
}

model UserBlock {
  id         String   @id @default(uuid())
  name       String
  category   String
  block_json Json
  userId     String
  user       User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt  DateTime @updatedAt
}

model MediaAsset {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  filename  String
  mime_type String
  size_bytes Int
  url       String
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt
}

model User {
  id              String           @id @default(uuid())
  email           String           @unique
  name            String?
  templates       Template[]
  designVersions  DesignVersion[]
  userBlocks      UserBlock[]
  createdAt       DateTime         @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime         @updatedAt
}

model Template {
  id              String           @id @default(uuid())
  name            String
  user            User             @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
  userId          String
  versions        DesignVersion[]
  currentVersion  DesignVersion?   @relation("CurrentTemplateVersion", fields: [currentVersionId], references: [id])
  currentVersionId String?          @unique
  createdAt       DateTime         @default(now())
  updatedAt       DateTime         @updatedAt
  designTags      DesignTag[]
}

model DesignVersion {
  id          String    @id @default(uuid())
  template    Template  @relation(fields: [templateId], references: [id])
  templateId  String
  design_json Json
  version     Int
  notes       String?
  createdBy   User      @relation(fields: [createdById], references: [id])
  createdById String
  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now())

  @@unique([templateId, version])
  templateAsCurrent Template? @relation("CurrentTemplateVersion")
}
